references.text: Moses gives a command to keep the statutes when they enter the promised land, the same theme of obedience in the new land.
It concerns entering the land that the Lord gives them and performing a specific service/ceremony.
Israel's first Passover celebration in the promised land, fulfilling the promise to observe this service when they entered the land.
God's promise to give the land of Canaan to Abraham and his descendants, the basis for the promise mentioned in Exodus 12:25.
God's promise to bring the people out of Egypt and into a good land, the background for 'as he promised'.
A parallel text that also deals with keeping the Passover service when they enter the promised land.
The book of Hebrews refers to Moses' faith when he instituted the Passover and the application of blood.
This verse in Deuteronomy provides the historical context for when the Passover practice from Exodus is to be introduced upon entering Canaan.
Both verses belong to the same legislative sequence concerning the Passover and the entry into Canaan, where 13:11 confirms the promise as the basis for the practice in 12:25.
